title: Filtering with different tests
idea: TOOL: the same filter shape works with any true/false test — even, below a limit, equal to a value. Swap only the condition.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

nums = [2, 5, 8, 11, 14]
evens = []
for n in nums:
    if n % 2 == 0:
        evens.append(n)
print(evens)
exercises.explanation: n % 2 == 0 is true for even numbers. 2, 8 and 14 pass, so evens is [2, 8, 14]. Only the test changed — the shape is the same.

exercises.prompt: To filter for something different, you usually change only the if condition — the empty list, loop, and append stay the same.
exercises.explanation: The filter shape is reusable. The test is the one part that decides what gets kept, so that is what you swap.

exercises.prompt: Which test keeps only the ODD numbers?
exercises.explanation: An odd number leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2, so n % 2 == 1 is the odd test. (n % 2 == 0 would be even.)

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

temps = [30, 18, 25, 12, 28]
hot = []
for t in temps:
    if t >= 25:
        hot.append(t)
print(hot)
exercises.explanation: t >= 25 keeps 30, 25 and 28. They are appended in the order they appear in the list.
'Equal to' is the == comparison (two equals signs). A single = would try to assign, which is a common mix-up.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

nums = [4, 7, 4, 9, 4]
fours = []
for n in nums:
    if n == 4:
        fours.append(n)
print(fours)
exercises.explanation: Every item equal to 4 is kept — duplicates included. There are three 4s, so fours is [4, 4, 4].

exercises.prompt: You want to keep scores between 5 and 10 inclusive. Which test does that?
exercises.explanation: 'Between 5 and 10' needs BOTH conditions true, so you join them with and. Using or would let almost everything through.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

nums = [3, 6, 9, 12, 15]
kept = []
for n in nums:
    if n % 3 == 0 and n > 5:
        kept.append(n)
print(kept)
exercises.explanation: All of these divide by 3, but the extra test n > 5 drops the 3. The rest pass both tests, so kept is [6, 9, 12, 15].

exercises.prompt: A filter test can combine conditions with and / or, just like any other if.
exercises.explanation: The if inside a filter is an ordinary if. You can combine conditions with and / or to make the test as precise as you need.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a filter that keeps only the even numbers from nums.
exercises.explanation: Empty list, loop, the even test with %, append the passers, then print. Same shape as every filter — only the test is special.
